subject: Audit proxy: tokenized artifact sharing & access model
messages:
From: Ryan Cole <ops@penfirm.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia@redbridgeconsult.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test artifacts — secure escrow / access model

Neha,

Thanks again for the call earlier. ProofPoint's security team has a compliance request: for a recent internal pentest they need an auditable, short-term escrow of artifacts (raw findings, reproducer scripts, and signed report) to be stored by a neutral partner so internal legal + audit can retrieve on-demand for third-party review. They also want fine-grained, time-limited access (per-request tokens) and an immutable access log.

Can Redwood operate an "audit-proxy" concept where artifacts live encrypted with a customer-provided KMS key and PenFirm or AuditWorks can request a tokenized one-time access window? Key constraints from ProofPoint:
- No permanent external storage without customer KMS control
- Access requests must be approved by ProofPoint's security admin or a delegated auditor
- Retention default is 90 days unless otherwise agreed

We're trying to model options with minimal legal churn. Any chance you can propose an ops model + SLA? We'll need to pass it to ProofPoint's procurement this week.

Attachments: none (report referenced in call).

—Ryan
Ryan Cole
CTO Ops
PenFirm Security
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Cole <ops@penfirm.io>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia@redbridgeconsult.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test artifacts — secure escrow / access model

Ryan — thanks, and apologies for the slightly delayed follow-up. High level: yes, Redwood can offer a tokenized audit-proxy pattern that satisfies the KMS and access-audit constraints. Broad proposal below; happy to iterate.

Summary proposal (ops model)
- Storage: Artifacts encrypted at rest with customer-supplied KMS key (we do not hold unencrypted copies).
- Escrow operator: Trusted third-party storage (AuditWorks) as the physical escrow; encryption and token gating managed by Redwood's control plane inside the customer's VPC or via a private connector for Dedicated customers.
- Tokenized access: Short-lived signed URL flow (OAuth-backed) with single-use tokens; token issuance requires a signed approval event (API call or signed e-mail) from the customer’s security admin.
- Audit trail: Immutable event log (append-only) surfaced in Redwood Console plus export to customer SIEM / supplied webhook.
- Retention: default 90 days; can be reduced to 30 days or extended to 365 on contract.
- SLA: access request turnaround: 4 business hours (standard) / 1 business hour (escalated) for on-call support (can be negotiated into Dedicated contracts).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Marcus and I will draft a concise operations runbook and a retention matrix for ProofPoint to review (includes roles, approval flow, token lifecycle).
2) Olivia: can you confirm AuditWorks' willingness to act as the escrow storage operator under these constraints?
3) Ryan: if OK, we'll route a short DocuSign SOW/NDA to get the legal language in place.

I'll attach a draft retention matrix and access procedure in the next email.

—Neha Kapoor
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Looping in Vanessa for SLA and retention policy sign-off. Quick notes:
- We should avoid making retention >90 days by default unless there's a paid add-on; longer retention increases legal exposure and storage costs.
- Token single-use enforcement needs guardrails: if we use signed URLs + KMS-wrapped keys, we can ensure there's no leakage but the customer must rotate KMS keys when they want removal.
- Need to align pricing (per artifact GB + per access request) and who pays AuditWorks storage fees.

Vanessa — any redlines on SLA targets and the request-turnaround times? I'll attach the rough retention matrix I promised.

—Marcus

Ryan / Olivia — thanks for the patience. Attached are: retention-matrix.xlsx (proposed defaults + optional tiers) and access-procedure.pdf (technical flow + approval API). Key contractual bullets we need in an SOW:
- Customer KMS ownership clause (customer retains key material; Redwood stores only ciphertext).
- Single-use token guarantee + replay protection; logs retained 7 years for audit purposes (can be scoped shorter if customer requests).
- SLA: 99.9% availability on token issuance API; access request turnaround 4 business hours standard / 1 hour for severity-1.
- Escrow operator fees: customer billed separately to AuditWorks; Redwood will coordinate issuance but does not bill storage fees unless agreed.

Please confirm: if Procurement accepts the retention default (90 days) and the token SLA, we'll issue a short SOW and a DocuSign link for signatures. I am attaching a redlined SOW template (summarized in the doc).

Attachments: retention-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), access-procedure.pdf (pdf)

- They also want the access-approval to be possible via a signed email when the named security admin is temporarily unavailable; can this be captured as an "approved delegate" flow in the runbook?
